amphora_molecule_property_finding.answer: Yes - and it is the only one of the nine whose binding is broken twice over - but the repair is not a pure repair, and its dry run cannot be planned today.
amphora_molecule_property_finding.chicken_and_egg_note: amphora-phase0-reviewer refuses to review a module whose recorded benchmark does not reproduce (verify_recorded_benchmark), so no fresh review can be obtained against the broken authoritative tree. That is precisely why the ceremony rehearses in a scratch copy: the replacement receipt is deterministic, so the reviewer can verify and sign it there, and the authoritative tree is touched exactly once.
honest_caveats: it has nothing to supersede on the review side: no independent-review receipt and no movement event exist, so the archive holds only the prior evaluation receipt and the prior benchmark result

because the tool demands dual identity, repairing it necessarily grants it its FIRST independent review - a state change beyond repair. Its phase does not change (PRE_PHASE_0 before and after), but it becomes promotable, which it never was
there is no smaller governed option: the tool will not, and should not, rewrite evidence on one signature
amphora_molecule_property_finding.question: amphora-molecule-property has no independent-review receipt and no movement event, so verify_module_with_replay/verify_evaluation_result take the live re-execution branch. Can re-evaluate help it at all?
amphora_molecule_property_finding.what_a_repair_would_do: re-evaluate regenerates both from one live evaluation, so both checks pass at once. Once the mandatory fresh review is imported, review_exists becomes true and the live branch is skipped, so the repaired binding is as durable as the other eight - it no longer re-breaks when module-manifest.json or config/benchmark-lock.v1.json legitimately change.
amphora_molecule_property_finding.why_its_binding_is_doubly_broken: verify_evaluation_result checks metrics.benchmark_result_sha256 against the shipped bytes for every module. For a module with neither a review receipt nor a movement event it ALSO re-executes the locked benchmark and compares the live diagnostic with first_replay.diagnostic_receipt. amphora-molecule-property fails both: pinned fc5a505c7e88c931842abaaebe0d4b2373f1d580c9b7b1ff2523a46a0a25c923 vs actual d04b516c806f452556ccdc91250d6ee2474f09565ac1656a88cbf13776716f90, and the shipped bytes are the MODULE-HARNESS shape, which carries no comparable diagnostic.
amphora_molecule_property_finding.why_no_dry_run_numbers: the dry run refuses before it can compute the replacement hashes, because no review receipt exists for this module anywhere. Supplying another module's review reproduces the cross-module refusal recorded in the table. No review was fabricated: signing a review receipt asserting independent_reimplementation_passed would be a false attestation. A human obtains the real one in the step-1 rehearsal, exactly as for the other eight, and only then can this module be planned.

count_reconciliation.question: config/program/phase0-decision-report.v2.json reported phase0_count 10 while the verifier derives 9.
count_reconciliation.why: phase0_count is not an independent fact. amphora-cli/src/phase0.rs::regenerate_report calls portfolio_status(), which calls verify_module_with_replay() for all 29 modules and writes the result to config/program/phase0-decision-report.v2.json. The report is a GENERATED artifact - control.rs::phase0_generated_file names it explicitly - and it is rewritten only when a mutating Phase-0 command runs (prepare / reissue / evaluate / review / promote / status --all --write-report). The B2 harness clobber changed shipped evidence WITHOUT going through any of those commands, so the report was never refreshed and kept describing a portfolio state that no longer existed on disk.

exact_human_command.summary: One governed command touches the authoritative repository. Everything before it happens in a scratch rehearsal copy and produces the fresh independent-review receipt that the governed command demands.
exact_human_command.why_a_rehearsal_is_needed: The fresh review receipt must bind evaluation_receipt_hash == sha256 of the receipt the repair will write, and amphora-phase0-reviewer only signs a receipt it has verified on disk. The replacement receipt is a deterministic function of the worktree (bundle bytes, parent hashes, claim locks, the two locked-benchmark replays, and a deterministic Ed25519 signature), so it can be produced in a copy first. `re-evaluate --dry-run` publishes that exact hash in advance, and the governed command refuses if the supplied review binds anything else - so a mismatch can only ever produce a refusal, never a bad write.

tool.command: portfolio phase0 re-evaluate --module <M> --reason <text> --as-of <YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ> --evaluation-key <external key> --review <signed review path> [--dry-run]
entry_points: plan_re_evaluation() - every refusal, computed before any mutation
re_evaluate() - the single governed mutation, backup + rollback
compose_evaluation() - the shared, write-free computation of the replacement bytes
evaluate_signed() - the single legitimate writer of benchmark/result.v1.json

movement_event_handling.result: the module lands at PRE_PHASE_0 / promotable and its phase must be re-derived by the existing `phase0 promote` command; the repair never mints a movement event
movement_event_handling.what: the prior movement event and ledger are superseded into the same archive and the ledger is reset to zero events
movement_event_handling.why: a movement event binds evaluation_receipt_hash. A replacement receipt therefore invalidates the prior movement claim, and verify_module_with_replay hard-bails ("movement event binding or filename is invalid") rather than merely failing a gate - which would break portfolio status for all 29 modules.

tool.rollback: the module tree is copied to .phase0-reevaluate-backup-<module>-<prior-sha> before the first mutation and restored (and the decision report regenerated) if any step fails
tool.single_writer_preserved: evaluate() previously resolved the evaluator identity from the environment and then wrote the evidence inline. It now resolves the identity and delegates to evaluate_signed(), which holds the only write_json_immutable call for evidence/phase0/benchmark/result.v1.json. re_evaluate() calls the same evaluate_signed(); no second writer was introduced. The write-free half was factored into compose_evaluation(), so a dry run predicts byte-for-byte what the real run writes.
